name: Week 30 Pull — Short, Pulldown Steps to 170, and the Curl Bottom Gets Softer
description:
**The short third day, same length.** Chest-supported row, reverse fly and cable crunch stay out.

**Lat pulldown steps to 170.** Four weeks at 160, and the last one was easy on almost no sleep while the pull-up has not moved. If 170 walls up, 160 is right there and going back is not a failed week.

**The incline curl keeps 25 and changes its bottom.** The left tendon is noticeable in daily life now, so the pad goes steeper and the reps stop just short of a locked-out elbow — the load stays, the provocation goes. **The light bicep set before the bar stays, and gains a 30-second hold.**

**The cable curl ladder moves up a rung: 220 → 230 → 240 → 250.** **DB row holds 75 → 85 → 95** and takes the spotlight.

dayOverview.theme: One load goes up, one bottom position gets softer, and the rest repeats. The pulldown finally steps off 160. The incline curl keeps its weight but stops living at full extension. The row gets the spotlight because its left-side ceiling is the one number in this day that needs a clean read.

spotlights.why: Last week the left grip broke a set earlier than usual, the day after the RDL took grip to failure — and you said it did not feel pre-cooked. With the RDL down at 45 this week, nothing is borrowed from the day before. This is the clean read.
Five weeks of the same left tendon spot, now noticeable outside the gym. The load is not the problem and is not moving; the bottom of the rep is the problem and it is.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W31 — spotlight moves to the lat pulldown at its new number and the face pull. W32 — chest-supported row and cable crunch return when the week stops being short.
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: pull-ups, DB row, lat pulldown, incline curl. Grip and position lifts where the honest ceiling is the rep the cue breaks.
🔥 near-failure last set OK: face pull, high cable curl. Isolation work where form holds at the limit.

**⭐ THE INCLINE CURL IS CHEST-SUPPORTED, PREACHER-STYLE.** Bench at ~45°, lean in chest-first, **armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad**, arm hanging down the **face** of the pad. The upper arm never lifts off. (The last three weeks described this wrong in the file — this is the version you have actually been doing.)

**This week the pad goes a notch STEEPER and the reps stop just short of straight.** A more upright pad means less strain on the tendon at the bottom, and the last few degrees of extension are where an irritable tendon gets poked. **Everything else about the lift is unchanged, including the 25s.**
**Tendons want load, not rest.** Keeping the weight is the treatment. If it ever becomes real pain, or the arm goes actually weak, that is different — say so.
**Pulldown: 170, and 160 is not a failure.** If the form breaks or the eccentric shortens, drop back mid-session and log it.
**Long rests on the pull-ups are yours to keep.** Four even sets on full rest is a fine shape. Write the numbers, do not chase them.
**Band-pull-apart is the pull-day shoulder anchor.** Keep the warmup lean — no extra band volume.

sets.name: Warmup (Pull-Up Bar Station) + Bicep Pre-Load
sets.notes: Lean by design. **The bicep pre-load worked, so it stays and grows slightly** — a light set plus one still hold, before anything hangs off the elbow.

exercises.notes: **The shoulder anchor for pull day.** Light band, slow, squeeze the blades together without shrugging.
Passive hang. **Also your first read on the right shoulder today** — note whether it is quiet.

**It helped, so it stays — and it gets one addition.**
- **Light DBs, nowhere near failure, left side first**
- **Then hold a light DB still at about 90° for 30 seconds on the left**, and the same on the right
- The hold is the point: a still, moderate load is the calmest thing you can hand an irritable tendon, and it goes in before the bar takes your bodyweight
**Protective activation — do this before anything loaded.** 40-50lb pair, behind the back, straight up and down, squeeze at the top.

sets.name: Pull-Ups — Straight Bar, 4 Sets, 3s Eccentric, Long Rests 🛑
sets.notes:
Bodyweight, 4 sets to form failure, **3s eccentric on every rep.** Straight bar. **Take the full 2 minutes between sets — the wall clock version you started doing yourself.**

- The set ends when the tempo breaks or the shoulders shrug up
- **Log all four numbers without chasing them**
- Four even sets and one big set then a fade are the same total work; either is a fine answer
- Three sets is fine if the shoulder is talking

exercises.notes:
Bodyweight, 4 sets, **3s eccentric every rep.** Straight bar, 2 min rest.
- Pack down before the elbows bend
- Set ends when the tempo breaks
- Write the numbers, leave them alone

sets.name: 🔆 DB Rack / Bench Block — Incline Curl → DB Row (3 Rounds)
sets.notes:
Both live at the adjustable benches — set up once and stay there.

**🔆 TWO SPOTLIGHTS, one station.** The curl is changing its bottom position to settle the tendon; the row is being read clean for the first time in a month now that the RDL is not eating the grip the day before.

**Reflection:** did the steeper pad and the short-of-straight bottom change what the left arm felt during the curl? And on the row — where did the left grip actually end this week?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 25lb both arms, 3 sets of 10 each side. **Left first.**

🔆 **Set-up, properly stated:**
- **Incline bench at ~45°, lean into it chest-first**
- **Armpit and the back of the upper arm flat on the pad**, arm hanging straight down the **face** of the pad
- **The upper arm never lifts off the pad** — if it does, this has become a standing curl

🔆 **The two changes this week, both about the bottom:**
- **Set the pad a notch STEEPER than usual** — more upright means less strain on the tendon at full extension
- **Stop a few degrees short of a locked-out elbow at the bottom.** Keep the tension, skip the very end of the range
- Slow eccentric still, and **arrive at the bottom — never drop into it**
- No shoulder swing to start the rep

**The 25s are not the problem and they are not moving.**

**LOAD:** pyramid **75 → 85 → 95**, one set each side.

🔆 **The clean read — nothing borrowed from yesterday this week:**
- **Chest supported on the bench**, spine long, no twisting to finish
- **Elbow drives back past the ribs**, not out to the side
- **Crush the handle from rep 1** rather than letting the grip fade in
- Slow eccentric, full stretch at the bottom
- **Log where the left ends on each of the three sets** — that is the number this week is for. No straps

sets.name: Lat Pulldown — 170 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** regular machine **170** · cable pulley **75/side**. **Log which.**

Four weeks at 160 and the last one was easy on almost no sleep. **If 170 breaks the form or shortens the eccentric, drop to 160 mid-session and log it** — coming back down is information, not a failure.

- **Pack the shoulders DOWN before the elbows move** — blades into the back pockets first
- Bar to the collarbones, chest up
- **Slow eccentric** — that is the part that should tell you whether 170 is real
- Ribs down, no leaning back to finish

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** regular machine **170** · cable pulley **75/side**. Log which.
- Pack **down** before the elbows bend
- Bar to the collarbones, chest up
- Slow eccentric, ribs down
- **160 is right there if 170 does not hold**

sets.name: Face Pull — 62.5 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 62.5, 3 sets of 20.

The third set went easy last week after biting for two weeks running — both of those were tired days. Same load; this is a well-placed number, not a stale one.

- **Hands finish beside the ears**, elbows high
- **Rotate the knuckles back** at the end of every rep
- Hold a beat, slow return
- Traps quiet

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 62.5.
- Hands finish beside the ears, elbows high
- **Knuckles rotate back** at the end of the rep
- Hold a beat, slow return, traps quiet

sets.name: High Cable Curl — 220 → 230 → 240 → 250 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **220 / 230 / 240 / 250** ascending · single pulley **67.5**. **Log which.**

**The ladder gains a rung at the top and drops the bottom one.** Four sets, same as always — the top step is new, the session length is not, and total curl volume stays where it is while the left tendon is irritable.

- **Single arm**, cable high, elbow fixed in space
- **Do not let the elbow drift forward** — the upper arm stays put
- Squeeze at the top, slow return to full extension
- **A short top set is the ladder working, not a miss**

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **220 / 230 / 240 / 250** ascending · single pulley **67.5**. Log which.
- Single arm, elbow fixed in space
- No elbow drift forward
- Squeeze at the top, slow to full extension
- Top set can run near failure

sets.name: Cool-Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block
sets.notes: Five minutes, every gym day. Slow breathing throughout — the downshift is as much the point as the tissue.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm, elbow at MID height.
Passive. Let the shoulders decompress after the pulling.

tips: Incline curl: armpit on the pad, arm down the face of it, pad a notch steeper, stop short of straight at the bottom.
The bicep warmup now ends with a 30s still hold on each arm.
Pulldown is 170 — and dropping back to 160 mid-session is a legitimate answer.
Log where the left grip ends on all three row sets. Nothing was borrowed from yesterday this week.
Cable curl ladder starts at 220 now. A short top set is the point of a ladder.
